newsitem.title: UK: UK institutions snap up Argentina's 2nd stg bond.
newsitem.headline: UK institutions snap up Argentina's 2nd stg bond.

text.p: Argentina launched its second sterling-denominated Eurobond on Thursday which saw strong British institutional demand and was oversubscribed, syndicate officials said.
"Argentina achieved the main objective of the deal which was to access the UK institutional investor base," syndicate official at joint lead manager UBS said.
"Many funds bought emerging market paper for the first time as they were looking for a 10-year maturity and it opened up new doors for emerging market product in the UK," he added.
The 200 million stg 10-year Eurobond was priced to yield 280 basis points over gilts and traded three notches tighter at 277 b.p. when the bond was freed to trade, dealers said.
"Argentina achieved attractive funding levels in sterling, very much in line with where they would have paid in dollars," UBS said.
There were also sales to retail investors in Continental Europe -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- who were attracted by the 10.0 percent coupon.
HSBC was the other lead manager.
Argentina is rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service and BB by Standard and Poor's.

Argentina's debut sterling-denominated five-year Eurobond was priced to yield 390 b.p. over gilts last July and has since tightened to trade around 210 b.p, dealers said. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
